bull.b: Consistent, high free cash flow (~$831M TTM and ~96% of net income) provides durable internal funding for R&D, launches, and M&A without heavy reliance on equity issuance. That cash convertibility supports strategic optionality and financial flexibility over the next several quarters.

bull.t: Very high margins and improving profitability
bull.b: Extremely high gross margins (~98%) and expanding operating/net margins indicate strong pricing power and operating leverage tied to a low-cost product mix. These durable margin characteristics help sustain earnings through revenue swings and fund continued pipeline investment.

Simultaneous commercial strength across INGREZZA and Cranesity plus acquisition of Soleno (adding VYKAT XR) and an active pipeline (multiple Phase 1/2 starts and 2027 readouts) create multiple durable growth engines, reducing dependence on a single product and supporting medium-term revenue resilience.

bear.b: The $2.9B Soleno acquisition financed in part by a $1.0B five-year revolver (initial $600M draw) increases short-term leverage and introduces covenant constraints tied to coverage/leverage metrics. This can limit financial flexibility for additional M&A, buybacks, or discretionary spend during integration.

Historical variability in revenue growth creates forecasting uncertainty and implies results rely on timing of launches, milestone recognition, and product adoption. Such uneven cadence can complicate resource planning and temporarily pressure margins if commercialization costs jump ahead of steady top-line gains.

Cranesity remains early in penetration (~10% of addressable CAH market) with initial prescribers treating few patients; combined with Q1 gross-to-net pressure and recurring INGREZZA payer seasonality, these dynamics pose sustained commercial and margin risks as broader prescriber conversion and reimbursement stability must materialize.
